This patch release reduces small-read and directory-entry metadata overhead
while preserving the existing API, snapshots, hooks and concurrency guarantees.

## Highlights

- `File.Read` explicitly unlocks its two return paths, reducing the deferred
  unlock wrapper work on small reads. The same mutex still protects the closed
  check, content access and cursor update.
- Directory entries without a regular-file hook own an immutable metadata
  snapshot that `Info` returns directly, avoiding another allocation per call.
  This also applies to directory entries when a hook is configured. Returned
  metadata stays usable after the entry slice or directory handle is discarded.
- Regular-file entries with hooks keep their lazy per-entry result, including
  concurrent initialization, cached errors and replay of a hook panic. Listing
  names still does not run hooks, and callbacks execute outside internal locks.
- The English and Chinese documentation now distinguishes captured stored
  metadata from lazy hook metadata, identifies each performance baseline, and
  records release verification steps.

## Measured results

The local comparison used **Go 1.27.3, darwin/arm64, Apple M5,
`GOMAXPROCS=1`**, with six adjacent AB/BA pairs per scenario in one binary
(`-benchtime=200ms -count=1 -cpu=1`). It compared the runtime implementation in
this release with published v1.1.0
(`d69c7500e0034579d72819a2a05cda1f97de960e`). Percentages use the median of
paired ratios, not the ratio of separately computed medians.

- Opening a fresh 4 KiB file, reading through EOF in 64 B chunks and closing it
  took **16.7% less time**. The 16 B and 256 B chunk cases improved similarly;
  allocation remained **128 B and one allocation per operation**.
- Listing 1,000 entries and calling every `Info` took **26.9% less time**.
  Allocation fell from **144,512 to 80,512 B/op (44.3% less)** and from
  **2,002 to 1,002 allocations/op**.
- Names-only listings retained their previous allocation counts. Repeated
  no-hook `Info` calls became allocation-free; fresh hook listings plus every
  `Info` were approximately unchanged in time and allocations.

These measurements describe specific microbenchmarks, not application
throughput. In a separate paired comparison with original `soulteary/memfs`
v0.1.0, the 1,000-entry listing plus every `Info` took about **18.9% less time**,
while the 64 B chunk read still took about **48% more time**. This release keeps
the per-handle synchronization absent from the original implementation. The
original comparison uses a static tree and independent handles.

See the [performance notes](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.1.1/docs/PERFORMANCE.md#v111-small-reads-and-entry-metadata)
for workloads, reproduction commands, allocation data and limitations.

## Installation

Requires **Go 1.27.3 or newer**, unchanged from v1.1.0.

```sh
go get github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit@v1.1.1
```

```go
import memfs "github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit"
```

There are no third-party Go module dependencies. The module path and package
name are unchanged.

## Compatibility and validation

No exported methods or signatures change. Snapshots, error behavior, content
ownership, hook paths and timing, per-listing caches and synchronization are
preserved. `Seek`, `ReadAt` and `Close` retain their existing behavior. Wrappers
that override `Open` still need to handle promoted `Stat` and `ReadDir` methods;
see [optional-interface dispatch](https://github.com/soulteary/memfs-kit/blob/v1.1.1/docs/PERFORMANCE.md#wrappers-and-optional-interfaces).

Validation includes Linux, macOS and Windows tests, the full race-enabled suite
with **97.9% statement coverage**, 15-second/two-worker path fuzzing, formatting,
vet, module checks and a smoke run of every benchmark. New regression tests
cover read/cursor boundaries, shared-handle byte consumption, retained file and
directory metadata, and hook panic caching. They also pass against v1.1.0 to
check that the existing contracts are preserved.
